llm.summary: The skill's code and runtime instructions are consistent with a local, static security linter for OpenClaw skills and do not request unrelated credentials, installs, or elevated persistence.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (security scanner for OpenClaw skills) matches what the code and SKILL.md do: static scanning of ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills and ~/.openclaw/skills, risk scoring, and optional SHA256 inventory. Required tools listed in SKILL.md (find, grep, sha256sum, etc.) are exactly those the included shell script uses.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the bundled shell script to scan skill directories and produce text/JSON output. The script performs static analysis (grep-based pattern checks) and computes SHA256 hashes; it does not execute scanned code or perform network calls. It limits scanning to files found under each skill directory (default roots) and flags but does not follow symlinks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or external downloads are present; the skill is delivered as a small shell script and docs. There are no URLs, package installs, or archive extraction operations in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The scanner looks for hardcoded-secret patterns inside files (e.g., AWS key regexes) but does not read or require runtime secrets or external keys.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled, does not request elevated privileges, and does not modify other skills' configurations. Autonomous invocation remains possible (platform default) but is appropriate for an on-demand scanner.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with its stated purpose: it is a local, static linter implemented as a shell script that scans skill directories and computes risk scores and optional SHA256 inventories. Before installing or running it: (1) review the included bin/claw-lint.sh (it is the scanner itself) to verify its behavior for your environment; (2) run it without sudo and, if you are concerned, run it in an isolated/test account so it only reads your skills directory; (3) note that the tool looks for hardcoded secret patterns and flags symlinks — it does not execute scanned code or contact the network. If you want stricter guarantees, run it on a copy of your skills directory rather than against your live ~/.openclaw/skills workspace.
